brief.subject: IRS withdraws part of spin-off proposal; year-end tax rule checks
brief.headline: IRS Partially Withdraws Section 355 Proposal; Key Year-End Tax Rules to Check
brief.dek: The IRS pulled back part of its proposed spin-off rules, plus reminders on installment sales, fuel tax records and disaster losses.
brief.lede: The IRS has partially withdrawn proposed regulations on tax-free corporate stock distributions under Section 355. Closely held corporations weighing a split should watch for revised guidance.

sections.heading: IRS Scales Back Spin-Off Proposal
bullets: The IRS partially withdrew proposed Section 355 rules on the device prohibition and active trade or business test.
Those tests decide whether a corporation can distribute a controlled subsidiary's stock without recognizing income, gain or loss.
Corporations and their shareholders and security holders are affected, so owners planning a split should revisit their timelines.

sections.heading: Big Installment Sales Carry Interest
bullets: Section 453A adds an annual interest charge on deferred tax once a seller's installment obligations for the year top $5 million.
Owners selling a business on payment terms should model this cost before closing, not after.

sections.heading: Truckers: Keep Four Years of Records
bullets: The IFTA Procedures Manual requires licensees to keep distance and fuel records behind each return for four years.
Missing mileage or fuel logs can leave trucking businesses exposed if a fuel tax audit arrives.

sections.heading: Disaster Losses Can Move Back a Year
bullets: Losses suffered in a federal disaster area may be claimed on the return for the year before the event.
That option can speed up a refund, though not every casualty loss qualifies for relief.

brief.seo_description: IRS partially withdraws Section 355 spin-off rules, plus the $5 million installment sale interest rule, IFTA record-keeping and disaster loss timing.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance Under Section 355 Concerning Device and Active Trade or Business; Partial Withdrawal
items.snippet: This document partially withdraws a notice of proposed rulemaking containing proposed regulations regarding the application of the device prohibition and the active trade or business requirement for distributions of controlled corporation stock (or stock and securities) by a distributing corporation without income, gain, or loss. The proposed regulations would affect corporations and their shareholders and security holders.
